title: Opa (tubular gourd)
summary: The opa is a long tubular gourd open at both ends, played by Idoma women for their own amusement. The lower end is beaten against the forearm or thigh while the other hand rhythmically covers and uncovers the upper opening, making a pulsing note.
howToPlay: Three places are lit: Beat on the body of the gourd, Cover at the wide mouth, Open when the mouth is freed.
A ring closes on the place to strike. A pad closes over the mouth on the Cover.
Keep the beat steady and let the mouth make the pulse.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: It matches the shantu of the Hausa, a similar long tube gourd, and is played for pleasure rather than at public events.
